sections.skill: Calculate a reorder point and balance stock against cash

questions.prompt: What is safety stock?

choices.text: Inventory locked in a safe for security reasons only
Items set aside to be thrown away later
A small extra cushion of inventory
Stock the owner keeps for personal use at home

questions.correct_answer: A small extra cushion of inventory
questions.intro: INVENTORY is the stock of goods or materials you hold to sell. Too little and you run out; too much ties up cash and risks damage or items going out of style. A REORDER POINT tells you when to order more: reorder point = average daily use x lead time (days to arrive) + SAFETY STOCK (a small extra cushion). Example: you sell 4 mugs a day, delivery takes 10 days, safety stock is 10: reorder point = 4 x 10 + 10 = 50 mugs. Count stock regularly so records match the shelf.

questions.prompt: What is 3 x 9 + 5?
questions.intro: Reorder point uses the order of operations: multiply first, then add. Daily use x lead time tells how many items sell while you wait for delivery. Then add safety stock. Example: 6 a day x 7 days = 42, plus 8 safety = 50. A common mistake is adding first: (6 + 7) x 8 = 104, which is wrong. Check by asking whether the answer is about one delivery-wait of sales plus a little extra.
